real_fix_mechanism: Per-monitor DPI + coordinate-space fix: WindowsFunctions.GetActiveDisplay now uses GetDpiForMonitor(MDT_EFFECTIVE_DPI) instead of GetDpiForWindow; PowerAccent.GetDisplayCoordinates returns raw/physical coords (no longer divides by DPI) and GetDisplayMaxWidth now divides physical width by DPI to get logical px; Selector.xaml.cs positions the window with SetWindowPos using physical pixels (plus off-screen pre-move to kill flicker, OnDpiChanged handler, selection-reset fixes). Also adds GetAsyncKeyState-based IsShiftState fallback and XAML/UI glitch fixes.
notes: Candidate was more precise on the true root cause. Its only misses were the SetWindowPos physical-pixel positioning in Selector.xaml.cs and the shift-key GetAsyncKeyState fallback, plus a speculative work-area clamp that didn't happen; core DPI mechanism nailed → 1.0/1.0. Distilled knowledge clearly helped the candidate pinpoint the precise DPI functions and the physical/logical scaling direction; the baseline stayed at the plausible-but-shallower UI layer.
